issues.legal_issue: Parol evidence cannot establish a subsequent oral arrangement that modifies or rescinds a registered disposition of property or a disposition that the law requires to be in writing.
material_facts: The property owner executed a registered settlement deed conferring rights in the property on his children.
The appellant relied on an alleged later oral family arrangement that would have divested some beneficiaries of rights conferred by the settlement deed.
The settlement deed was both registered and a disposition that required writing to confer title effectively.
issues.conclusion: The alleged subsequent oral arrangement could not be proved by parol evidence, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 92 of the Evidence Act, including proviso (4), oral evidence generally cannot contradict, vary, add to, or subtract from the terms of a proved written instrument. Proviso (4) permits proof of a subsequent oral agreement to rescind or modify an earlier agreement only where the earlier disposition is not required by law to be in writing and has not been registered. A disposition required to be in writing, or a registered disposition, may be altered, rescinded, or varied only by a subsequent written instrument; the judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: property_disposition_dispute and oral_evidence_offered_to_change_terms and (registered_disposition or disposition_required_writing)

predicates.property_disposition_dispute: The proceeding concerns rights created by a disposition of property.
predicates.oral_evidence_offered_to_change_terms: A party offers oral evidence to prove a later oral arrangement that would change or rescind the disposition's terms.
predicates.disposition_required_writing: The disposition was required to be in writing to confer title effectively.

issues.definition: When a property-disposition dispute involves oral evidence offered to change the terms of a registered disposition or one required to be in writing, that evidence is inadmissible.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot obtain appellate consideration of a new characterization of a document where the parties agreed below on its characterization and the case proceeded on that basis.
material_facts: At trial, the parties agreed that the instrument was a settlement deed rather than a will.
The trial court proceeded on the basis of that agreement.
On appeal, the appellant argued that the instrument was a will.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to entertain the appellant's argument that the instrument was a will.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the procedural consequence of the parties' agreement and the basis on which the case was tried, declining to consider a contrary characterization first advanced on appeal. The judgment cites no provision or earlier case for this point.

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a civil case.
predicates.parties_agreed_below_on_document_charact: The parties agreed in the lower court on how the document was characterized.
predicates.case_proceeded_on_that_characterization: The lower court decided the case on the basis of the agreed characterization.
predicates.appellant_raised_contrary_characterizati: The appellant advanced a contrary characterization of the document on appeal.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, when the parties agreed below on a document's characterization and the case proceeded on that basis, a contrary characterization raised by the appellant is not entertained.
